title: Wang2016 – SSVEP Wang 2016 dataset
description: A benchmark steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) dataset comprising EEG recordings from 34 healthy subjects performing a 40-target brain-computer interface speller task using joint frequency and phase modulation. The dataset includes 64-channel EEG data sampled at 250 Hz with visual stimuli flickering at frequencies ranging from 8 to 15.8 Hz, designed to facilitate the development and evaluation of SSVEP-based BCI algorithms.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a Synamps2 system (Neuroscan, Inc.) at 1000 Hz sampling rate with 64 channels positioned according to the international 10-20 system, referenced to vertex (Cz). A notch filter at 50 Hz was applied during recording. Continuous EEG was segmented into 6-second epochs (500 ms pre-stimulus, 5.5 s post-stimulus) and downsampled to 250 Hz. Subjects performed a cue-guided target selection task with 40 visual stimuli flickering at different frequencies, completing 6 blocks of 40 trials each.
